title: HyperDet Wavefunction: A Phase-Agnostic Ansatz for Strongly Correlated Systems
authors: Xiaodong Hu, Guan-Lin Lin, Ying Ran, Di Xiao
abstract: Describing competing phases of strongly correlated systems often requires trial wave functions built from phase-specific assumptions. We propose the \emph{hyperdeterminant (HyperDet) wavefunction} as a phase-agnostic ansatz for both bosonic and fermionic quantum many-body systems exhibiting spontaneous symmetry-breaking order, fractionalization, and/or topological order with anyonic excitations. The HyperDet structure emerges naturally by fusing auxiliary fermionic parton Slater determinants into physical orbitals through a fully learnable \emph{fusion tensor} $\mathcal F$. Optimized using variational Monte Carlo, a single HyperDet architecture can achieve exceptionally high overlaps $\geq 99.9\%$ with exact-diagonalization ground states throughout the entire fractional Chern insulator phase in both bosonic and fermionic models, and across their nearby competing phases. We introduce the singular-value spectrum of the \emph{bipartite fusion matrix} as a structural diagnostic of fusion tensor, and find that its redistribution tracks many-body phase transitions without computing phase-specific observables. The optimized fusion tensor also encodes the parton-level topological data: it reproduces the parton Chern numbers expected for the bosonic and fermionic FCI states, completing their field-theory descriptions and the resulting topological order. Its intrinsic gauge structure further determines whether physical symmetries admit virtual lifts and, when faithful lifts exist, extracts their projective class; for the bosonic FCI, this recovers the expected parton translation fractionalization. We thus anticipate the HyperDet wavefunction to be a promising variational platform for both accurate ground-state searches and phase-diagram explorations across strongly correlated phases, and for providing interpretable theoretical insights from parton-level microscopics to field-theory descriptions.
summary: This paper introduces the HyperDet wavefunction, a novel, phase-agnostic ansatz for strongly correlated quantum systems. It uses a learnable fusion tensor optimized via VMC to achieve high accuracy across various correlated phases, including FCIs. The method's key strength is its ability to diagnose topological order and phase transitions by analyzing the tensor's structural properties, such as its singular-value spectrum.
main_problem: Developing a robust, phase-agnostic trial wavefunction ansatz for strongly correlated quantum many-body systems exhibiting spontaneous symmetry-breaking order, fractionalization, and/or topological order.
main_result: The proposed HyperDet wavefunction achieves high accuracy ($\geq 99.9\%$) across diverse correlated phases, and its structure naturally encodes parton-level topological data and tracks phase transitions via its singular-value spectrum.
method: The ansatz is constructed by fusing auxiliary fermionic parton Slater determinants into physical orbitals using a fully learnable fusion tensor, optimized via Variational Monte Carlo.
model_or_system: The method is applied to strongly correlated systems, specifically focusing on Fractional Chern Insulators (FCIs) in both bosonic and fermionic models, and tested on the extended Fermi-Hubbard model on a checkerboard lattice.
key_observables: Wavefunction overlap with exact-diagonalization states, singular-value spectrum of the bipartite fusion matrix, parton Chern numbers, and the connected static structure factor $S(\mathbf{q})$ (for CDW diagnosis).

main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the fusion tensor can be learned variationally to capture the necessary physics across different phases, and that the method can be extended to include internal degrees of freedom.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure of the HyperDet wavefunction and show the connected static structure factor $S(\mathbf{q})$ exhibiting sharp Bragg peaks in the candidate CDW phase, alongside finite-size scaling of the charge gap.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the HyperDet ansatz using a fusion tensor, details the variational optimization using VMC, and then applies the framework to diagnose and characterize multiple phases (FCI, AHC, CDW) in the extended Fermi-Hubbard model using various diagnostic tools.
why_interesting: The phase-agnostic nature and the ability to extract topological invariants and symmetry information directly from the learned tensor structure make it a powerful, general tool for understanding complex correlated phases beyond simple mean-field assumptions.
